title: The Benefits of Small Language Models (SLMs) | Cohere
gist: Cohere argues enterprises are moving away from single large-LLM deployments toward portfolios that pair small, task-specific models with large ones, citing its own Command R7B, Tiny Aya, and North Mini Code as benchmark-beating examples of cost, latency, and sovereignty advantages.

insights.claim: Enterprises are shifting away from an either/or choice between large and small models toward building model portfolios that assign specific tasks to the model best suited for them (a 'right-sizing' approach).
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: AI infrastructure spend is likely to fragment across multiple model sizes/vendors rather than consolidate around a single frontier-model provider, favoring orchestration and multi-model tooling plays.
insights.quote: The reality for most enterprises isn't an either/or choice between large and small models. Instead, leaders are building model portfolios that strategically combine both.

insights.claim: Cohere frames the 'bigger is better' era of AI as ending, predicting enterprise AI strategy will default to matching model size to task requirements rather than defaulting to the largest available model.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Vendors selling only frontier-scale models risk losing enterprise workloads to cheaper task-specific models; watch for growth in small/open-weight model adoption as a leading indicator.
insights.quote: The era of "bigger is better" in AI is giving way to a more nuanced approach, where model size is strategically matched to task requirements.

themes.theme: Benchmark Evidence Small Models Beat Larger Rivals

insights.claim: North Mini Code is a 30B-total-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with only 3B active parameters, purpose-built for agentic software engineering, and can run locally on a MacBook without requiring paid API calls.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Local-inference coding models reduce enterprises' dependence on per-token API spend with large cloud LLM providers, a cost lever for dev-tooling budgets.

insights.claim: On Artificial Analysis' Coding Index, North Mini Code scored 33.4, outperforming several much larger models including Qwen3.5 (35B-A3B), Gemma 4 (26B-A4B), Devstral Small 2 (24B Dense), Nemotron 3 Super (120B-A12B), Mistral Small 4 (119B-A6B), and Devstral 2 (123B).
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: A 3B-active-parameter model beating 120B+ models on a third-party coding benchmark undercuts the assumption that raw scale predicts task performance, a data point for evaluating coding-copilot vendor claims.
insights.quote: On Artificial Analysis' Coding Index, North Mini Code achieves a score of 33.4, outperforming numerous larger models

insights.claim: Tiny Aya, a 3.35B-parameter model trained on 70 languages with region-aware post-training, has a 'Global' variant that outperformed Gemma3-4B in translation quality in 46 of 55 languages on the WMT24++ benchmark.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Sub-4B multilingual models beating a similarly sized competitor across most of 55 languages suggests translation/localization workloads can be shifted to cheap small models rather than large general-purpose LLMs.
insights.quote: Tiny Aya Global outperforms Gemma3-4B in translation quality in 46 of 55 languages on WMT24++

insights.claim: Cohere's smallest enterprise offerings span Command R7B (7B parameters, its fastest Command R model), the Tiny Aya family (3.35B parameters) for multilingual deployment, and North Mini Code (30B total / 3B active) for coding, indicating Cohere's small-model line targets three distinct enterprise workloads.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is positioning a multi-model small-model product line (chat/general, multilingual, code) as a competitive wedge against single-model large-LLM vendors.

insights.claim: Compute and memory needed for fine-tuning scale with parameter count, such that a 218B-parameter model needs dramatically more GPU memory to fine-tune than a 7B model, letting small-model users run more experiments in resource-constrained environments.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Fine-tuning cost curves favor small-model iteration speed; enterprises optimizing for rapid experimentation cycles should weight small-model TCO advantages over raw large-model capability.
insights.quote: a 218B-parameter model needs dramatically more GPU memory to fine-tune than a 7B model

insights.claim: For organizations with thousands of users, small per-user cost savings from using right-sized models can translate to millions of dollars in reduced operational expenses at scale.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Per-seat AI cost reduction compounds materially at enterprise scale, making small-model routing a measurable line item for CFOs evaluating AI ROI.
insights.quote: For organizations with thousands of users, small cost savings per individual can translate to millions in reduced operational expenses.

insights.claim: Many companies are now allocating budget toward AI infrastructure costs rather than personnel costs, reflecting how expensive it has become to run large models at scale.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: A shift in enterprise cost structure from headcount to AI compute spend is a trend worth tracking in corporate opex breakdowns and IT budget surveys.
insights.quote: Many companies are now allocating resources to AI costs rather than personnel costs due to the significant expense of running large models at scale.

insights.claim: Cohere frames small-model strategy around three enterprise risks: costly integration overhead, employee habits of defaulting to large/expensive models, and lack of governance over token and agent usage.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Enterprises adopting small models need parallel investment in usage governance tooling, not just model swaps, to realize the promised cost savings.

insights.claim: Cohere North is positioned as a monitoring system that tracks token consumption, agent usage, and testing to give enterprises predictability in AI spend and prevent cost overruns via per-task token limits.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Governance/observability tooling for AI spend (token metering, agent activity monitoring) is emerging as a necessary companion product category to model deployment.

insights.claim: Because small models run without cloud dependency, they support on-premises, private cloud, and on-device deployment, which Cohere positions as key for meeting sovereign AI and data-residency requirements in regulated industries.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Regulated-industry buyers (finance, healthcare, government) are a distinct addressable market for small/on-prem models where large cloud-API LLMs face data-sovereignty friction.

insights.claim: Enterprises can run Cohere models in their own VPC or on-premises environment, or through a dedicated Model Vault, giving them control over security, infrastructure, and data — a deployment option Cohere offers alongside usage-tracking governance features.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Model Vault/VPC deployment is a concrete product differentiator for Cohere versus API-only competitors when selling into data-sensitive enterprise accounts.
insights.quote: enterprises can run Cohere in their own VPC/on-premises environment or through a dedicated Model Vault, giving them control over security, infrastructure, and data
